dedupe_keys.name: catalog of space debris clouds jonathan s space report

description: The Catalog of Space Debris Clouds lists the events that produced significant numbers of catalogued debris objects in Earth orbit, from a 1961 Ablestar residual-propellant breakup onwards, and groups tracked debris into clouds that share a parent object and broadly similar orbits. Jonathan McDowell compiles it as part of Jonathan's Space Report, in the same spirit as NASA's History of On-orbit Satellite Fragmentations but with a slightly different list of clouds and new plots. Each row gives the parent piece, event date and type (for example residual propellant, battery, deployment or collision), event perigee, apogee and inclination, the number of catalogued pieces and height and inclination ranges, with per-cloud height-history and Gabbard-style plots and orbital maps. Coverage is global Earth orbit; the data was last updated on 22 June 2025 at reading. Format and access: HTML tables and plots on a public website, with column and plot documentation. Licence: McDowell's catalogues are published under CC BY 4.0; free. Caveats: only clouds with enough catalogued objects are listed, and the association of late-discovered objects with a cloud is inferred. It supports hazard exposure analysis of debris for satellite infrastructure. Related catalogue records are GCAT, the ORDEM debris model and the LEGEND evolutionary model.
